characteristics.cultivar: Local landrace cultivars (Xiao Bai / non-Da Bai)

description.short: A medium-bodied white tea between Bai Mu Dan and Shou Mei, historically presented as tribute to the imperial court
description.overview: Distinguished from Bai Mu Dan by traditionally using local landrace tea bushes (such as Xiao Bai) rather than specialized large-bud cultivars like Da Bai.
description.leaf: Bud with medium-sized leaves, slightly smaller than those of Bai Mu Dan
description.aroma: Floral and hay-like, gentle and mellow
description.taste: Medium-bodied, bridging Bai Mu Dan and Shou Mei, with a delicate sweetness
description.processing: Plucking buds with leaves from local landrace bushes → withering → slow drying without fixation

history.origin: The name translates to 'Tribute Eyebrow' — historically, although crafted from ordinary local bushes rather than elite cultivars, its quality was deemed fine enough for imperial tribute.
history.development: Long regarded as an intermediate grade bridging prestigious Bai Mu Dan and everyday Shou Mei.
history.modern: Less prevalent on the international market today than Bai Mu Dan or Shou Mei, it remains an official standard category in Fujian white tea classification.
interestingFacts: The primary technical distinction of Gong Mei from Bai Mu Dan is its origin from traditional local landrace bushes rather than large-leaf Da Bai/Da Hao cultivars.
In practice, commercial boundaries between Gong Mei and Shou Mei can vary across producers, occasionally leading to overlap and confusion even among tea specialists.
